chunks: And it is narrated from Jarrah al-Mada'ini, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a house in which there are three rooms, and they do not have enclosures.
He said: "Permission pertains only to the rooms; there is no permission required for the house."

key_terms.أَبْيَاتٍ: rooms or inner living quarters within the house
key_terms.الْبُيُوتِ: the rooms or living quarters for which permission is relevant
key_terms.الْمَدَائِنِيِّ: the attribution of the narrator Jarrah to al-Mada'in
key_terms.دَارٍ: a house or dwelling as a whole

ai.seo_question: When is permission required for entering rooms within a shared house?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about seeking permission in a dwelling that contains multiple rooms without separate enclosed courtyards. The Imam عليه السلام clarifies that the relevant permission concerns the individual rooms, not merely the larger house as a whole.
